title: Saying What Is Fair, Normal or Strange

sections.title: Judging, not announcing
sections.content: You know *importante*, *necesario* and *lástima* from A2 Unit 27: *es importante que*, *es necesario que*, *es mejor que* and *es una lástima que* all take the subjunctive. An expression that gives your opinion about something takes *que* + subjunctive, even when the thing is real: you are judging it, not announcing it. At B2 you add a wider range of judgments, and you use them with other tenses.

sections.title: More judgments that take the subjunctive
rows: Conviene que hablemos con la jefa.
es justo / es injusto / es razonable que
Es razonable que pidan más tiempo.
es lógico / es normal / es comprensible que
Es inaceptable que nadie avise a los vecinos.
Es raro que no conteste el teléfono.

sections.title: Past events
sections.content: You know *haya* from B1 Unit 37: use *haya* + participle for something that has already happened, and the imperfect subjunctive when the judgment is about the past.

items.spanish: Es injusto que hayan cambiado el horario sin avisar.
items.english: It is unfair that they have changed the schedule without warning.

items.spanish: Era lógico que los clientes quisieran una respuesta rápida.
items.english: It was logical that the customers wanted a quick answer.

items.spanish: Es ridículo que tengamos que esperar tanto.
items.english: It is ridiculous that we have to wait so long.

items.spanish: Es razonable que pidan más tiempo para el proyecto.
items.english: It is reasonable that they ask for more time for the project.

sections.content: Compare a fact with a judgment. *Es verdad que los precios suben* states a fact, so it takes the indicative. *Es injusto que los precios suban* gives an opinion about the same fact, so it takes the subjunctive.
